# Ramen

> Governed MCP for teams: a self-hosted MCP platform that enforces an organisation's security and structure on every tool call (SSO roles per group, NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails per tool, promptfoo evals and NVIDIA SkillSpector scans gating deploys, Arize Phoenix traces per person, audit). Self-hosted, multi-zone, highly available MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for Kubernetes on GKE (GCP), EKS (AWS) and AKS (Azure, since 0.7.5). A git repo of Python tools, resources and prompts becomes a fleet of MCP workers behind a cloud load balancer. A Rust node speaks Streamable HTTP (`POST /mcp`) and JSON-RPC 2.0 over gRPC on one port, serving MCP spec 2026-07-28 (stateless requests, standard headers, multi round-trip requests, tasks) and 2025-06-18 on the same endpoint since 1.0; a Python 3.12 runtime runs the code with optional per-tool guardrails (NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails rails or a `policy.py`, before the call and after the result); a FastAPI console manages groups, environments, zones, secrets, canary deploys, roles per group and custom roles, OAuth 2.1 sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID and Google Workspace groups (identity federation), autoscaling of workers between 1 and an admin-set max, IP rules, throttling and audit. Since 1.0 an idle zone can sleep at 0 workers behind an activator pod that wakes it on the first authenticated call, a deploy can build a group's worker image from its `requirements.txt`, and nodes export OpenTelemetry spans and counters (never arguments or results) with optional per-group caller consent. Since 1.0.0 a group repo also carries promptfoo evals, NVIDIA SkillSpector-scanned skills, MCP Apps, LLM configs and guardrails, each a client policy every call must carry (`-32024`…`-32029`); LLM rails, evals and scans reach providers only through the console's LLM judge proxy (`/llm/v1`); every in-cluster hop is TLS with a per-install CA and plaintext is refused on cloud installs. The 1.0.0 release candidate ran live on GKE (with a satellite cluster), EKS and AKS on 2026-11-17/18 (demo deploy with evals 6/0 and SkillSpector SAFE, a tool call through each load balancer, the full verification suite with one outdated test assertion per cloud that passed once corrected, load tests with p95 under 1.5 s on all three, Entra ID sign-in with the groups lookup on AKS; the Google Cloud Identity group lookup ran live with a consumer Google account, while mapping a looked-up Google group to a role is tested against a fake only and a Workspace-domain account was never tried). BSD-3-Clause. Version 1.0.1.

Clients send `Authorization: Bearer rmk_<group key>` or a console-issued OAuth token, plus `ramen-group` and `ramen-zone` headers the load balancer routes on. Standard MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code / GitHub Copilot, the mcp SDK) connect directly over HTTP with a group key; Claude Code also signs a person in with OAuth 2.1 + PKCE (`claude mcp add-json … "oauth":{"clientId":…}`; the console is the authorization server; no dynamic client registration, so Cursor, VS Code and Claude Desktop sign a person in through the bridge). Stdio clients use `ramen-mcp-bridge` (PyPI; `uvx ramen-mcp-bridge@latest`, e.g. `claude mcp add <name> -- uvx ramen-mcp-bridge@latest --target <edge>:443 --tls --oauth https://<edge> --client-id <id> --group <g> --zone <z>`), which carries a key (`--key`) or signs the person in with `--oauth`; the bridge (since 0.3.0) keeps tokens in memory (or `--keychain`), forgets them after 30 idle minutes and returns a needed sign-in as JSON-RPC error -32001 with the URL. The group page generates these commands per install. Tools live in a git repo under `mcp/tools/<name>/<name>.py` + `<name>.json`; deploys sync the repo to a bucket, roll a canary worker, smoke-test, then roll stable.

## Docs

- [Home](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/): what Ramen is, the three repos, why
- [Wiki overview](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/): one page per subject
- [Try the demo / Get started](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/get-started/): a step-by-step walkthrough for beginners, from installing Docker to a governed MCP server on a laptop: the demo group, a guardrail blocking a call, an MCP client with a key and with OAuth, traces in Phoenix, the audit log; what needs a cluster (evals, scans, sleeping zones)
- [Deploy your first group](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/first-group/): from an empty console to a tool call, with the engines, evals and scan results, LLM configs acceptance and Phoenix
- [Roles](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/roles/): super admin, group admin, viewer, MCP user, custom roles and group keys, what each may do
- [MCP features](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/mcp-features/): every MCP capability a worker serves (tools, resources, templates, prompts, tasks, MRTR, subscriptions, MCP Apps, Skills over MCP) and how a group repo codes it, with the demo repo's code
- [IAM and network on GCP](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/iam-network-gcp/), [AWS](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/iam-network-aws/), [Azure](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/iam-network-azure/): every identity and permission, NetworkPolicies, firewall / security group / NSG rules, the edge
- [How it works](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/how-it-works/): the architecture and every feature with where it is managed
- [Deploy on GCP](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/deploy-gcp/): Terraform, images, Helm, first zone and group, the console's service account and access controls, teardown
- [Deploy on AWS](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/deploy-aws/): the same on EKS with DynamoDB, S3, Secrets Manager and an ALB
- [Deploy on Azure](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/deploy-azure/): the same on AKS with Table Storage, Blob Storage, Key Vault and an Envoy Gateway edge
- [Groups, zones and regions](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/groups-zones/): the model, deploying, scaling, rebalance, per-tool access, blocked packages, IP rules
- [Autoscaling](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/autoscaling/): Ramen scales workers between 1 and a max per zone (no HPA): decision rules, cooldowns, audit, load-test results on GKE, EKS and AKS
- [Guardrails](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/guardrails/): `mcp/guardrails.yaml`, NeMo Guardrails rails or a `policy.py`, per tool, pre and post, fail-closed
- [Sleeping workers](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/sleeping-workers/): `sleep_after_secs` per group × zone, what idle means, the activator pod, the first call held up to 25 s then `503` with `Retry-After`, cost, audit
- [The MCP repo](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/mcp-repo/): layout, the JSON contract, resources and prompts, secrets in code, local testing
- [Worker images](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/worker-images/): the release image, an image built on deploy from `mcp/requirements.txt` (kaniko Job into the group's own repository as its own `ramen-build-<group>` identity, pinned by digest; `RAMEN_BUILD_*`), or a pinned one; precedence and failed builds
- [Telemetry](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/telemetry/): OTLP/HTTP export (`mcp <method>` spans, `ramen.mcp.calls`/`errors`, `ramen.deploy`), what agents are told (`telemetry` in the token answer, `_meta["io.ramen/telemetry"]`), consent per group and its error codes
- [Multi round-trip requests](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/mrtr/): MCP 2026-07-28 tools that ask the client for input (`InputRequired`, `elicit`, `sample`, `list_roots`) and are called again; signed `requestState`, guardrails on every round, what a 2025-06-18 client sees
- [Tasks](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/tasks/): `"task": true` tools and the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension: lifecycle, `tasks/get|update|cancel`, the Redis task store, limits
- [Secrets](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/secrets/): scopes, `{{$group.NAME}}`, `mcp/env.yaml`, backends
- [Users and access](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/users-access/): roles per group, custom and OAuth-only roles, memberships from the IdP and from admins, service-account permissions, audit and logs
- [Connect with OAuth](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/connect-oauth/): registering a client; Claude Code over HTTP; Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop through the bridge; bridge token storage
- [Connect with a password](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/connect-password/): a password account through the same flow
- [API keys and the API](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/api-keys/): `rmk_` versus `rmn_`, the OpenAPI page at `/api/docs`, a cheat sheet
- [Throttling with Redis](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/throttling/): per-IP and per-token limits shared across zones
- [Entra ID and Google Workspace](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/sso/): providers on the Config page, group lookup through Microsoft Graph or Cloud Identity, role rules by group id, OAuth-only roles, troubleshooting (AADSTS50011)
- [Backups](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/backups/): create, preview, restore, prune, reconcile
- [Deploy from GitHub Actions](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/deploy-github-actions/): a least-privilege `rmn_` API key as a repo secret, a workflow that deploys the group on push and waits for the job
- [Configuration](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/configuration/): the config file, the public address (base URI) and running behind a path-prefix proxy, the state store, every variable that matters, restricting actions
- [Changelog](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/changelog/), [Releases](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/release/), [Version tracker](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/versions/)
- [Transport, hop by hop](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/transport/): what protects each hop, the two protocol versions (2026-07-28 and 2025-06-18), standard headers, `server/discover`, subscriptions, what is verified and what is not
- [Threat model, security and isolation](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/threat-model/): trust boundaries, what a group can reach, secrets at rest, the gate codes, every security finding with its status
- [Agent skills](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/skills/): Agent Skills (agentskills.io) an agent installs to deploy Ramen on GCP, AWS and Azure, verify and tear it down, rotate keys, back up, scale, test and fix the code
- [Contributing](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/contributing/): build, test and modify each component
- [Interface contracts](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/CONTRACTS/)
- [Architecture](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/architecture/): components, data model, decisions

## Code

- [ramen](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen): console/ (FastAPI), node-rs/ (Rust, tonic), runtime-py/ (Python), proto/, deploy/ (compose, Helm, Terraform, CloudFormation), skills/, tests/
- [ramen-mcp-bridge](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen-mcp-bridge): the stdio bridge, `uvx ramen-mcp-bridge@latest` or `pip install ramen-mcp-bridge` (1.0.0, the bridge for Ramen 1.0.0: TLS by default and the policy versions)
- Images: `docker.io/bkraad47/ramen-worker` and `ramen-console` (also `ghcr.io/bkraad47/`), tags `<version>` and `latest`, linux/amd64 and arm64; the local compose stack pulls them
- [ramen-demo-mcp-group](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen-demo-mcp-group): the demo group repo: tools (one asks before it acts, one runs as a task, Iris data tools on pandas), resources, prompts, an MCP App, two skills, an `env.yaml`, golden cases, NeMo rails (static and LLM), promptfoo evals and LLM configs
- [Releases](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen/releases)
- [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen/discussions): questions, ideas, show and tell; forks and contributions welcome (BSD-3-Clause)
